title: Dawn runbook clipboard & incident follow-ups - Sasha
content:
(Scratchpad — early shift)

Goal: capture quick follow-ups from last night's pages, queue actionable runbook TODOs, and note sanity checks before handing to day SRE. Keep short, prioritize items with owner + ETA.

SUMMARY OF PAGER EVENTS (06:30–10:00)
- 06:42 AM: High 5xx spike observed on hosted inference API (route: /v1/generate). Brief spike to 18% 5xx, reverted within 9m after auto-fallback to model-variant small-3b.
  - Pager: alert-5xx-rate (threshold crossed).
  - Initial mitigation: routing fallback triggered, traffic split adjusted by runtime.
  - Impact: ~1200 requests failed briefly; customer-reported errors: 5.
- 07:15 AM: Redis primary eviction storm in eu-west-1 (ttl queue backlog). Latency for KV cache read up to 300ms for a 15-min window.
  - Pager: alert-redis-latency-high.
  - Mitigation: scaled Redis read replicas + flush of stale prefix cache keys for tenant-549.
  - Side-effects: transient increased token cost (more model calls).

NOTES / OBSERVATIONS
- Pattern: both incidents correlated with a sudden spike in long requests (seq len > 1024) from a single customer key (tenant-549). Suspect malformed workload or synthetic test from them.
- Runtime logs show repeated KV cache misses (req_id example: req_6f7a2c) preceding the redis latency alert.
- Auto-fallback to small-3b helped reduce 5xx but didn't fully avoid elevated latency for streaming responses.

IMMEDIATE FOLLOW-UPS (high priority)
1) Tenant-549 contact + throttle request
   - Owner: Morgan Wu (oncall sales/syseng contact)
   - Action: ask customer to pause burst or provide new req samples; request they throttle to 20 rps while we investigate.
   - ETA: 2026-10-12 EOD
2) Add short-term rate-limiter rule at ingress for abnormal seq_len > 1024 from a single API key
   - Owner: Sasha Patel
   - Action: draft rule in API gateway; implement in staging; roll to prod as canary
   - Quick command to test locally: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <tenant-549-key>" -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate -d '{"input":"...","max_tokens":12000}' | jq .
   - ETA: 2026-10-12 midday
3) Redis topology hardening
   - Owner: Diego Ramos
   - Action: review eviction policy for prefix caches; add monitoring threshold for evictions/sec; consider RDB/AOF check
   - ETA: 2026-10-14

RUNBOOK TODOS (medium priority)
- runbook:redis-failover: add a step to identify tenant-specific keyspace hot-keys (script outline below)
  - Script sketch: redis-cli --scan --pattern "pref:tenant:549:*" | xargs redis-cli ttl | sort -n
  - Add instructions to rotate prefix cache for a tenant in <5m with minimal impact.
- runbook:api-fallback: record recent auto-fallback thresholds/metrics and ensure the console shows the active fallback variant and reason (add link in UI).
- add note under "cost.exeptions" to attribute cost bump when fallback to bigger model fails (tags: billing-impact).

LONGER-TERM ACTIONS (backlog)
- Implement workload-class detection (synthetic vs prod) via UA and request pattern; propose a small classifier in the routing layer (PR draft in infra: PR#901).
- Evaluate prefix-caching TTL defaults per tenant tier; documented thresholds in confluence.

QUICK COMMANDS / INVESTIGATION ARTIFACTS
- Get recent 5xx traces: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://observability.api/trace?service=api&label=5xx&since=30m" | jq .|less
- Redis metrics snapshot (eu-west-1): kubectl -n infra exec redis-primary-1 -- redis-cli info stats | egrep 'evicted_keys|keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses'
- Check routing decisions for req_id: kubectl -n runtime logs router-5 -c router | grep req_6f7a2c -n -A5

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Did tenant-549 run a bulk synthetic test (CI job)? Need to confirm with account team. (Morgan)
- Was cache key TTL misconfigured for them, or did they change their app causing many unique prefixes? (Diego)
- Are our fallback thresholds too aggressive for preserving latency vs cost? (Product/Platform discussion)

HANDOFF NOTES FOR DAY TEAM
- TL;DR: tenant-549 burst caused cache hot-keys -> redis evictions -> increased KV misses -> latency -> some 5xx. Temporary mitigations in place (fallback + scaled replicas). Prioritize talking to customer and applying ingress throttles if bursts continue.
- Check console alerts: open alert-5xx-rate (alerts panel) and the redis-latency-high alert; link threads in ticket JIRA-4881.
- If redis evictions persist after replica scaling, consider RPO: promote a warm replica or trigger a controlled flush of tenant prefix keys (see runbook:redis-failover step 4).

MISC NOTES (personal)
- Coffee. Remember to eat.
- Follow up: Morgan to post customer note in #gcs-handovers; Diego to add eviction alarm to dashboard; Sasha to draft quick ingress rule PR and assign to release-engineering for canary deploy.

END OF SCRATCHPAD

(Will tidy up later and move persistent items to confluence & JIRA).
